title: Capture a real operator price twice per game week
problem: Every certification gate that depends on price fails, not because the signals are bad but because no verified opening or closing price exists anywhere in the repo.
option_a: Do nothing; keep the board permanently in paper and say so.
option_b: Capture one operator's NFL page on a fixed schedule (Tuesday and three hours before kickoff), store the raw snapshot with a UTC stamp, and populate MARKET_OPEN and MARKET_CLOSE from it.
option_c: Buy or licence a commercial odds history and ingest it.
evidence: price-store: 156 of 390 snapshot rows are empty, all for want of a publisher
review_test: If two consecutive weeks of captures produce an opening and a closing price for at least 90% of originated markets, this becomes the default and G2 becomes testable.

title: Rebuild the totals model before trusting any total or moneyline
problem: The totals model's out-of-sample MAE is statistically indistinguishable from always predicting the league average, yet the moneyline is derived from the side and the total together.
option_a: Keep the current model and publish the total with a health warning.
option_b: Rebuild it on pace and efficiency inputs, re-measure against the same naive baseline, and only then re-derive the moneyline.
option_c: Stop originating totals and price only the side and the moneyline.
review_test: If the rebuilt model does not beat the naive baseline by at least 0.5 points of MAE on a held-out season, take option C.

title: Grade parlays against an empirical joint, never independent legs
problem: The two-leg parlay family prices its legs independently; the board shows it needs 27.44% to break even and delivered 26.32% over 1,953 bets, so the independence assumption is doing real work.
option_a: Keep independent pricing and accept the error.
option_b: Require an empirical joint estimate for every leg pair, and refuse the bet when the market price assumes independence and we cannot measure the joint.
option_c: Drop parlays from the board until the joint can be measured.
evidence: strategies: S8 on the research board
review_test: If a measured joint for the most common leg pair differs from the independence product by more than the pricing tolerance, B is mandatory.

title: Extend the official results feed backwards to clear the sample gate
problem: The certification universe gives each family 4-51 graded bets against a 300-bet minimum, so nothing can be certified this season whatever its hit rate.
option_a: Lower G1 explicitly and record the increased false-discovery risk.
option_b: Accumulate seasons of official results with the same week-by-week transcription.
option_c: Accept that certification waits for future seasons and keep the board in paper.
review_test: If a second season of official results is transcribed and families still fall short of 300, revisit option A with the risk recorded.

title: Cap the multiplicity budget explicitly
problem: Holm and deflated-Sharpe corrections need an honest count of how many families were tried; an open-ended budget silently understates the correction.
option_a: Register every family before grading, including abandoned ones.
option_b: Set a fixed per-season family budget and hold to it.
option_c: Report the correction at several budget sizes so the reader sees the sensitivity.
evidence: strategies: nine families pre-registered, eight produced bets
review_test: If the number of tried families exceeds the declared budget in any season, the season's corrections are recomputed.

title: Wire the demotion gate into the build
problem: The six demotion triggers are defined but enforced by hand, so a gate that waits for a person is not a gate.
option_a: Leave it as a published rule.
option_b: Wire D1a-D1f into the build so a demotion is written to the ledger and the decision log without a human step.
option_c: Route demotions through a weekly review meeting.
evidence: gates: six triggers, none fired, all currently evaluated by hand
review_test: Inject a synthetic drawdown past the D1b threshold; if the build does not demote the strategy, the wiring is wrong.

title: Keep the prop-combo family on the board as an explicit blank
problem: S9 produced no bets because no prop lines exist; deleting it would make the board look complete when one of the three bet classes is simply unpriceable.
option_a: Delete S9 until prop lines exist.
option_b: Keep S9 with zero bets, the reason printed on the row, and the blocking flag linked.
option_c: Model prop lines from season medians so the row has numbers.
review_test: Option C is rejected in advance: modelled lines would be inferred values, which this repo does not publish.

title: Record an ADR row whenever a suggestion changes state
problem: Accepted suggestions without a recorded rationale get re-litigated and rejected ones get re-proposed.
option_a: Track decisions in the suggestions table only.
option_b: Append a dated decision row (decision, evidence, owner, revisit date) to a decision log whenever a suggestion moves.
option_c: Hold the decision in the pull request that implements it.
review_test: If the log has fewer than one entry per accepted suggestion, the process is not being followed.

title: Re-read the official injury report twice more per week
problem: Game status is empty for 301 of 326 rows at retrieval, so the replacement-depth tracker under-counts Out players early in the week.
option_a: One read per week, as now.
option_b: Read on Wednesday, Friday and Saturday; keep each snapshot and show the tracker's movement across the week.
option_c: Read only on Saturday, when statuses are fullest.
review_test: If the Saturday read adds no Out designation over the Friday read for two consecutive weeks, drop back to two reads.

title: Publish the reward structure as a proposal, not a commitment
problem: The brief asks for rewards, but cash prizes raise licensing, tax and eligibility questions that no public source answers for this project.
option_b: Run the competition as points-only until the reward and jurisdiction questions are answered, and publish the intended cash structure as a marked proposal.
review_test: Close the reward and jurisdiction questions first; then publish reward terms with eligibility rules attached.

title: Make the capture clock the product, not the model
problem: The desk can read game lines but cannot prove a price was available at a time; every CLV, gate and reward statement depends on that one missing property.
option_a: Add a second capture at a fixed weekday time (Thu 18:00 ET) and a third at kickoff-minus-60m, both stored with the raw block hash.
option_b: Capture continuously every 15 minutes and keep only the first and last observation per market.
option_c: Do nothing automatic; capture by hand whenever you look.
evidence: price_snapshots: one capture per game; flags F-01/F-02
review_test: If the operator starts serving a documented feed or the page blocks scheduled requests, switch to B or stop.

title: Publish a market-efficiency scorecard before any picks
problem: The model disagrees with the market by 1.8 points on average and up to 3.2 on the side; without a scorecard a reader cannot tell a missing variable from a mispriced game.
option_a: Publish, per market, the model's mean bias, mean absolute disagreement and residual variance against the closing price, with n.
option_b: Publish picks with a written argument for each.
option_c: Publish nothing until the model beats the market in backtest.
review_test: If mean absolute disagreement falls below the market's own week-to-week movement, the model is calibrated enough to justify picks.

title: Separate the two scoreboards physically, not just by column
problem: Signal and staking are two halves of one table; a reader skimming a green profit number will not notice a red signal verdict three columns to its left.
option_a: Two separate pages with their own navigation entries, and the staking page carries a banner showing the signal verdict for every row.
option_b: One page, staking columns collapsed by default behind a toggle.
option_c: Keep one table and rely on column order.
evidence: staking_masking_example: 25% hit rate, FAIL verdict, +31.8% bankroll
review_test: If the owner reads the staking view only and cannot state the signal verdict afterwards, the separation is not working.

title: Rank replacements by depth, and cap the metric before it is trusted
problem: Depth is measured in rungs, but only some charts are read and few slots are exposed; a ranking built on a handful of observations is a story, not a measurement.
option_a: Display depth per slot as a fact and suppress any club-level ranking until 32 charts are read.
option_b: Rank clubs now on the depth index and add a sample-size warning.
option_c: Combine depth with snap counts to estimate the quality drop.
review_test: If all 32 charts are read and at least 20 slots are exposed, promote B and revisit C.

title: Consolidate the overlapping desks into one readiness view
problem: Three desks answer the same brief (price snapshots, verified results, signal/staking) from different namespaces; a reviewer cannot see the state of every requirement in one place.
option_a: Add a fourth desk that re-implements the same gap.
option_b: Build a consolidated decision-readiness view that reconciles the desks and names the gate and clearing number for each requirement.
review_test: If a reviewer cannot answer 'what blocks requirement X, and what number clears it' from the landing page, the consolidation has failed.
